setup.name: Mobile Food Vending License (personal, 2 years)
setup.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)
setup.note: NYC Business: $50 for the two-year full-term license; free for honorably discharged veterans. Every person who works the cart or truck needs one, not only the owner. The DOHMH renewal form asks $60. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy. waitDays is my estimate: the license needs the DOHMH food protection course for mobile vendors and a visit to the licensing center.

setup.name: Mobile Food Vending Unit Permit (cart or truck, 2 years)
setup.note: NYC Business: $200 for a full-term two-year permit when food is prepared on the unit, $75 when it only sells pre-packaged food. The fee is tiny; the problem is the cap. You can apply only when DOHMH invites you from a waiting list. Local Law 18 of 2021 added 445 permits a year through fiscal 2026; the January 29, 2026 veto override adds 2,200 supervisory license applications a year from 2026 through 2031 (6sqft, Council press release). waitDays = 365 is my estimate of the wait after the list reopens; before 2026 the wait was measured in years and most vendors rented someone else's permit.

setup.name: Restricted Area Mobile Food Vending Permit (private property, no cap)
setup.note: NYC Business: new application $200 (food prepared on the unit) or $75 (pre-packaged), renewed every two years; no waiting list and no cap, but only on private property in a commercially zoned area, and it never covers street fairs. NYC311 adds park property under an agreement. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy. waitDays is my estimate.

setup.name: Food Protection Course for Mobile Vendors (DOHMH, with exam)
setup.note: $53 (Health Code fee and NYC Business), paid separately from the license; offered in English and Bangla; fail the exam and you pay again. The license arrives by mail about a week after passing. A free 15-minute online refresher is due every four years. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: New stainless coffee cart built to Health Department specs
setup.note: Toast's 2025 guide puts a food cart at $5,000-$10,000 before equipment and permits. A NYC coffee cart also needs a DOHMH-approved hand sink and water tanks, an espresso or brewing setup on a generator or propane, and it must pass the pre-permit inspection at the DOHMH Bureau of Food Safety garage. $15,000 = $9,000 for the body + $6,000 for brewing equipment, generator and tanks: my estimate, no NYC fabricator price list was found.

setup.name: Used food truck, fitted out and inspected
setup.note: Start Business by State (2026) puts a new truck at $100,000-$175,000. A used, already-fitted truck is my estimate at $90,000. Trucks also need commercial auto insurance, a DOT visual inspection and an FDNY LPG permit when they cook on propane.

setup.name: Commissary contract: first month and deposit
setup.note: DOHMH: every permitted cart or truck must be cleaned, serviced and stored at an approved commissary or depot, which holds its own non-retail permit; the commissary agreement is checked at the pre-permit inspection. Monthly prices seen: $250-$300 for garage space (Untapped Cities, 2013, old); vendor guides give $300-$3,000 a month. $1,500 = a $750 month + a $750 deposit, my estimate.

setup.name: FDNY Certificate of Fitness G-23 (propane for mobile cooking)
setup.note: FDNY: a G-23 holder must connect and disconnect LPG containers over one pound on a food cart or truck; the certificate needs a written exam. The renewal fee is $15 (NYC Business). The $25 application fee is my assumption: the excerpt did not show it. Not needed if the cart runs on a battery or generator only.

setup.name: FDNY permit: LPG on a mobile food truck
setup.note: FDNY LPG permit page: Transportation / Mobile Food Truck permit $105.00; a truck may carry at most two cylinders of no more than 100 lb each and needs a minimum 20:B-C extinguisher and a DOT visual inspection. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: Quiet inverter generator or battery pack for the cart
setup.note: My allowance for a 2-3 kW inverter generator or a lithium battery station; an espresso boiler draws 1.5-3 kW. Without power the cart sells batch brew from airpots only.

setup.name: Temporary Food Service Establishment Permit (street fairs, markets; 1 year)
setup.note: NYC311 and the DOHMH application packet: $70 a year (+$25 when making frozen desserts); it covers street fairs, flea markets and carnivals, expires one year after issue, and a supervisor with a Food Protection Certificate must be on site at all times. A cafe's own FSE permit covers only its own storefront. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: 10x10 tent, weights, folding tables, coolers, hand-wash station
setup.note: My allowance. Markets require a hand-wash station, a tent with weights and a fire extinguisher; electricity is extra (Appear Here listing for a Smorgasburg Saturday spot: $50 a day).

setup.name: Build-out of a 150-300 sq ft takeaway window or kiosk
setup.note: My estimate: 200 sq ft x $225 per sq ft (the standard food-space rate used in the cafe pack's extra.buildout). A window still needs a hand sink, a three-compartment sink, a mop sink and hot water; it drops the customer restroom (no seats), the dining furniture and most of the floor finish.

setup.name: Park or plaza concession: security deposit and first guaranteed fee
setup.note: NYC Parks licenses pay the greater of a guaranteed annual minimum or a share of gross receipts: Harlem Meer snack bar $20,000 in year 1 vs 9%; Cadman Plaza cafe minimum vs 10%; a 2025 FCRC item 11%; a February 2026 item 6%. $10,000 = half of a $20,000 first-year minimum held as deposit, my estimate.

setup.name: Full-size electric convection oven
setup.note: Vulcan VC6ED single-deck full-size electric convection oven, 208V 3-phase, 12.5 kW: $8,086.00 at WebstaurantStore. Countertop half-size units start near $900 (Avantco). Three-phase power is often missing in old storefronts: check the panel before you buy. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: Ventless rapid-cook oven (hot sandwiches without a hood)
setup.note: TurboChef Bullet, 208/240V: $17,190.00 at WebstaurantStore (Middleby list $17,191). It cleans its own grease vapor with a catalytic converter, so many cafes heat food without a Type I hood, but TurboChef itself says the final allowance depends on the local authority; in NYC that is DOB and FDNY. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: Type I exhaust hood, duct, fan and wet-chemical fire suppression
setup.note: One NYC data point: a 2025 DOB filing for a new Type I hood and exhaust at 852 Ninth Avenue lists $22,000 of work, without the suppression system, which is filed separately with FDNY and installed by a licensed master fire suppression piping contractor. $45,000 = $22,000 hood and duct + $8,000 suppression + $15,000 for the roof run, makeup air and the engineer's filing: my estimate. A long duct to the roof of a tall building costs far more.

setup.name: FDNY Commercial Cooking System permit
setup.note: FDNY: $70.00 to maintain or operate a commercial cooking system, plus acceptance-test fees for the fire extinguishing system. Duct cleaning above the hood must be done by an FDNY-approved company whose workers hold a W-64/P-64 Certificate of Fitness. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: Gas authorization for restaurant equipment (DOB) and Con Edison turn-on
setup.agency: NYC Department of Buildings and Con Edison
setup.note: NYC Business lists a separate DOB gas authorization for restaurant equipment, filed by a licensed master plumber. Cost: my allowance for the plumber's filing and pressure test. Wait: past NYC cases ran 3-6 months (Lucky Bee cooked on induction for three months; a 2017 State Senate survey found only 17% of businesses got gas service on time). Con Edison and the NYC Hospitality Alliance let you ask about gas availability before you sign a lease.

setup.name: Spiral dough mixer (60 qt class)
setup.note: My estimate for a commercial spiral mixer that kneads about 60-80 lb of dough; small cafes that bake only muffins and cookies use a 20 qt planetary mixer at a fraction of the price.

setup.name: Proofing cabinet / retarder
setup.note: My estimate. A retarder lets a baker shape dough in the afternoon and bake at 5 a.m. without a 3 a.m. start: it trades equipment money for labor at night.

setup.name: 48-inch refrigerated sandwich prep table
setup.note: Avantco APT-48-HC 47-inch two-door refrigerated sandwich prep table: $1,329.00 at WebstaurantStore (a MainStreet 48-inch mega top is $1,079; Traulsen $5,172). Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: 12-inch manual meat slicer
setup.note: Avantco SL512 12-inch gravity-feed slicer, 1/2 hp: $619.00 on sale at WebstaurantStore (heavy-duty Globe GC512 $2,976). Slicers are a top source of kitchen cuts and of Listeria findings when not taken apart and cleaned every 4 hours of use. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: Commercial cold-press juicer
setup.note: Goodnature X-1 Mini: about $11,900 on the Goodnature reseller page (more than 30 bottles an hour); the model has been replaced by the Hummingbird and a certified used unit sells for more in Australia. The page excerpt was ambiguous, so this stays an estimate.

setup.name: Two commercial drink blenders with sound enclosures
setup.note: Vitamix Drink Machine Advance: $474.96 on sale to $1,111.02 list at KaTom; quiet-enclosure models cost more. $1,900 = two machines at about $950, my estimate.

setup.name: Automatic cup sealing machine
setup.note: Toast: bubble tea sealers $1,000 to $4,000+; another guide lists automatic sealers at $1,460-$1,799, 300-500 cups an hour. Sealed cups also cut spills on delivery orders.

setup.name: Automatic tapioca pearl cooker, fructose dispenser, tea brewer
setup.note: Toast: automatic tapioca pearl cookers around $4,500 (simple 12 L pearl cookers sell for under $200 at Walmart). Fructose dispenser and tea brewer are inside this allowance, my estimate.

setup.name: Bubble tea franchise fee (optional brand)
setup.note: Gong Cha 2025 FDD as reported by aggregators: initial fee $40,000-$45,000, 6% royalty + 1% brand fund, total investment $184,500-$627,060; Kung Fu Tea 2025 FDD: total $169,000-$378,000 with a $25,000-$37,000 fee and 4% + 2%. I could not open the FDDs themselves.

setup.name: Six-week booth at a flagship holiday market
setup.note: Retail Brew (November 2023), with figures from the operator Urbanspace: Bryant Park Winter Village booths $22,500-$40,000 for the season, plus electricity. 2023 figures; Union Square premium spots cost extra.

setup.name: State Liquor Authority Restaurant Wine license (wine and beer, NYC, 2 years)
setup.note: SLA retail fee chart revised June 12, 2026: Restaurant Wine, New York City tier, $960 license fee for two years + $100 filing fee. Eligibility: ABC Law 3(27) defines a restaurant as a place regularly and in a bona fide manner used for serving meals, with a kitchen able to cook the assortment of foods ordinary meals need, in charge of a chef; SLA guidance asks for full entree-style meals whenever open. A pastry-and-sandwich cafe fits the Tavern Wine class instead (soups and sandwiches), which community boards resist more. Wait: the SLA's own notice estimated 24-26 weeks for new applications (Rodriguez Law), so 180 days. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: State Liquor Authority Tavern Wine license (wine and beer with light food, NYC, 2 years)
setup.note: For places that serve soups, sandwiches and the like rather than full meals (SLA guidance on food requirements). Fee: a NYC law firm's buyer guide gives $1,252 for two years ($1,172 per extra bar); another guide gives $1,152; I could not read the Tavern Wine line of the official June 2026 fee chart. Community boards in NYC are reported to resist tavern applications more than restaurant ones (Rodriguez Law).

setup.name: SLA Temporary Retail Permit (sell while the license is pending, 180 days)
setup.note: SLA temporary retail permit form (February 2026): $640 per bar for the initial 180 days for wine/liquor on-premises applications ($128 for beer-only, grocery and drug stores); 30-day extensions available. A 2024 law doubled the term from 90 to 180 days and removed NYC's rule that the premises must have been licensed in the last two years. The permit itself took 6-8 weeks in 2023-2024 reports (Bond Schoeneck & King), so 50 days. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

setup.name: 30-day notice to the community board, questionnaire and hearing
setup.note: Every on-premises applicant in NYC must notify the community board at least 30 days before filing with the SLA and attach proof of the notice. The board's vote is advisory, but boards attach stipulations (closing hours, no outdoor alcohol, no live music) that the SLA writes into the license. Fee: none; the cost is time and often a lawyer at the hearing.

setup.name: Wine fridge, glassware, beer kegerator and point-of-sale alcohol setup
setup.note: My allowance: a dual-zone wine refrigerator, a two-tap kegerator, 120 glasses and the till's age-check prompt. The SLA requires the licensed area to match the filed floor plan; moving the bar later needs an alteration application.

setup.name: Liquor license attorney or expediter
setup.note: My estimate for preparing the SLA application, the community board questionnaire and the hearing. Many small owners file themselves; errors restart the SLA clock.

setup.name: Shared or ghost kitchen onboarding: deposit, first month, insurance certificate
setup.note: Seen on The Kitchen Door: a Brooklyn shared prep kitchen at $3,700 a month (insurance and ServSafe required); Ozone Park $28-$48 an hour with 20 hours a month minimum; Nimbus Downtown Brooklyn $25-$40 an hour with 32 hours a month for three months. $3,500 = one month plus a deposit at the hourly end, my estimate.

setup.name: Delivery tablets, label printer, tamper-evident bags and opening packaging
setup.note: My allowance. Each delivery app ships its own tablet or integrates through one aggregator; tamper-evident bags cut 'missing item' refunds.

monthlyCosts.name: Commissary or depot (cart and truck storage, cleaning, water)
monthlyCosts.note: Required for every permitted cart or truck (DOHMH). $750 = middle of the $300-$1,500 range seen in vendor guides; old reporting found $250-$300 for garage space only (Untapped Cities).

monthlyCosts.name: Rented vending permit (illegal, see shortcut)
monthlyCosts.note: Queens Eagle, April 2025: vendors pay up to $25,000 every two years to rent a permit that costs its holder $200; one vendor paid $14,000; IBO cited $17,000+ a year. $850 a month = $20,000 / 24, the middle of those figures. Shown only so the shortcut has a real price.

monthlyCosts.name: Delivery app fees (basic plan)
monthlyCosts.note: NYC caps: 15% for delivery, 5% for the basic listing and 3% for card processing = 23% of each delivery order; Local Law 79 of 2025 lets apps sell an optional 'enhanced' package for up to 20% more (43% total). Applies to the delivery share of revenue only. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

monthlyCosts.name: Shared kitchen time (about 120 hours a month)
monthlyCosts.note: 120 hours x $35 an hour (listings in Brooklyn and Queens ran $25-$48 an hour). A full-time private ghost-kitchen station costs more and is quoted only on request.

monthlyCosts.name: Liquor liability insurance
monthlyCosts.note: Insureon: its small-business customers pay about $41 a month for liquor liability on average; New York's Dram Shop Act (General Obligations Law 11-101) makes the seller liable for injuries caused by a guest it served unlawfully, and NYC landlords usually demand the policy. $100 a month is my New York allowance for beer and wine.

monthlyCosts.name: Hood and duct cleaning plus fire-suppression service
monthlyCosts.note: FDNY: duct cleaning by an approved company; NFPA 96 tables set quarterly cleaning for high-volume cooking and longer intervals for light cooking; suppression systems are serviced every six months. $250 = about $1,800 a year of cleaning + $1,200 of suppression service, my estimate.

monthlyCosts.name: Concession fee to the park or landlord (share of sales)
monthlyCosts.note: NYC Parks cafe and snack-bar licenses: the greater of a guaranteed minimum or 6%-11% of gross receipts (Cadman Plaza 10%, Harlem Meer 9%). The guaranteed minimum is a separate fixed floor.

monthlyCosts.name: Franchise royalty and brand fund
monthlyCosts.note: Gong Cha: 6% royalty + 1% brand fund of gross sales (2025 FDD as reported). Only for a franchised bubble tea shop.

monthlyCosts.name: Propane refills for the truck or cart
monthlyCosts.note: My allowance. FDNY rules limit how much LPG a commissary may store and who may swap cylinders (a G-23 holder).

staff.name: Baker (early shift)
staff.note: BLS OEWS May 2023, New York-Newark-Jersey City: bakers' mean wage $19.40 an hour, 16,160 employed; a NYSDOL data mirror gives a New York City region median of $44,060 a year. $22 = the 2023 mean raised for 2026 and for a 4 a.m. start (no legal night premium in New York; the premium is what it takes to hire). NYC minimum wage in 2026: $17.00.

staff.name: Sandwich maker / prep cook
staff.note: My estimate: the $17.00 NYC minimum plus $2 to hold a lunch line. No 2026 metro statistic was found for this role.

staff.name: Evening server-bartender (wine and beer)
staff.note: Paid the NYC tipped food service cash wage of $11.35 with a $5.65 tip credit only if tips cover the gap and written notice is given (same rule as the cafe pack); otherwise $17.00. BLS OEWS May 2023: bartenders in the New York metro earned a mean $27.91 and a median $21.68 an hour including tips. Servers must be at least 18 under most sources; sources disagree on 21 for bartending.

staff.name: Cart or truck helper (licensed vendor)
staff.licenseRequired: Mobile Food Vending License ($50 / 2 years) and the $53 mobile vendor food protection course
staff.note: NYC minimum wage $17.00 in 2026 (NY DOL). Every person working the unit needs a personal vending license.

taxes.name: NYC retail beer, wine and liquor license tax
taxes.appliesIf: the business holds a State Liquor Authority retail license in NYC
taxes.note: NYC Department of Finance: 25% of the annual state license fee, due June 25 each year (new licensees by the 25th of the month after issue). For a Restaurant Wine license, $960 for two years = $480 a year x 25% = $120 a year. rate holds the dollar amount because the base is fixed. The Council suspended the surcharge for one year from June 1, 2022; I found nothing showing a suspension in 2026.

shortcuts.name: Rent someone else's cart permit
shortcuts.what: You skip the waiting list. The permit holder must be at the cart; if an inspector checks, the cart is seized and the permit can be revoked.
shortcuts.unlocks: start vending on the street now instead of waiting for the permit list; the rent to the permit holder (about $850 a month, monthlyCosts.black_market_permit_rent) is paid separately
shortcuts.savesNote: Compared with the legal private-plaza route (Restricted Area permit): no $600 monthly fee to the plaza owner (lever cart_spot) and full street demand.

shortcuts.name: Sell from a metered parking spot
shortcuts.what: The best curb on the block is a meter. Selling from it is barred; agents ticket and can tow.

shortcuts.name: Park the cart by the subway stairs
shortcuts.what: More people pass you, but you are within 10 ft of the entrance. Sanitation agents fine you and can break down the setup.

shortcuts.name: Pour wine before the license arrives
shortcuts.what: Evening sales start months early. It is a crime under state law and it can sink your pending application.
shortcuts.unlocks: evening wine and beer sales during the 2-6 months before the temporary permit or license
shortcuts.savesNote: Skips the $640 temporary retail permit: about $107 a month over its 180 days. The real gain is the evening revenue it unlocks.

shortcuts.name: Skip ID checks on busy nights
shortcuts.what: Faster service at the counter. One sale to a minor in a sting costs thousands and puts the license at risk.

shortcuts.name: Bottle juice without the warning label
shortcuts.what: You sell bottles to go without the unpasteurized-juice warning. The Health inspector cites it.

shortcuts.name: Put a fryer or griddle in without a hood
shortcuts.what: Hot food without a $45,000 hood. FDNY and the Health Department treat it as a fire hazard; a grease fire is uninsured.

shortcuts.name: Skip the fire-suppression and duct service
shortcuts.what: Saves the contractor visit. Grease builds in the duct; FDNY writes it up and insurers refuse fire claims.

shortcuts.name: Swap propane tanks without a certificate
shortcuts.what: No exam, no wait. FDNY can stop the truck on the spot.

shortcuts.name: Hand out plastic straws with every drink
shortcuts.what: Boba needs a wide straw and plastic is cheaper. Unrequested plastic straws break the city's straw law.

violations.name: Vending without a Mobile Food Vending License
violations.law: NYC Admin Code 17-307; Health Code Article 89
violations.criminal: Until 2025 a misdemeanor (up to $500 and 30 days); the 2025 law made it a civil violation of up to $1,000.
violations.note: 6sqft and NY1 on the July 2025 bill (Intro 47), override in September 2025: unlicensed vending becomes a violation with fines up to $1,000. Exact schedule not seen.

violations.name: Vending from a cart or truck without a unit permit
violations.law: NYC Admin Code 17-307; Health Code Article 89
violations.criminal: Civil since the 2025 decriminalization law; DSNY can still remove the cart and discard food it considers unsafe.
violations.note: News 12: DSNY keeps its civil powers to break down setups, fine and discard food. closureDays = 30 is my game value for getting the cart back and finding a legal permit.

violations.name: Cart worked under someone else's permit
violations.law: NYC Admin Code 17-307 (supervisory license holder must be present, Local Law 18 of 2021)
violations.criminal: Permit renting is the black market the 2021 and 2026 laws try to end; holders lose the permit.
violations.note: Local Law 18 of 2021 created supervisory licenses so that the permit holder stands at the cart. Fine: my assumption of the $1,000 unlicensed-vending maximum.

violations.name: Selling from a vehicle at a metered parking space
violations.law: 34 RCNY 4-08(h)(8); Monroy v. City of New York (2012)
violations.note: Appellate Division 2012: the rule covers food trucks. NYC Finance lists a $65 fine for parking at a meter to sell goods; the table was garbled in the excerpt. Repeat tickets plus towing make it a monthly cost.

violations.name: Cart too close to a crosswalk, subway entrance or door
violations.note: DSNY: next to the curb, 20 ft from building entrances, 10 ft from crosswalks, subway entrances and driveways, on sidewalks at least 12 ft wide. Civil penalties up to $250 for time, place and manner violations after the 2025 law (6sqft); the January 2026 package raises some siting penalties.

violations.name: Selling alcohol without a license
violations.criminal: A misdemeanor with up to six months in jail; it also counts against the pending license application.
violations.note: ABC Law 130(1): selling without an appropriate license is a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months. Fine amount not seen in the excerpt; $2,500 is my game value.

violations.name: Sale of alcohol to a person under 21
violations.criminal: The server can be charged; repeat offenses lead to suspension or revocation.
violations.note: SLA press release (April 2024): civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation, starting at $2,500-$4,000 for a first offense; the licensee is liable whether the owner or an employee served. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

violations.name: Unpasteurized juice bottled on site without the warning label
violations.note: NYC food service penalty schedule (Appendix 23-C) lists $400 and $600 for unlabeled unpasteurized juice packaged on premises, per the search excerpt.

violations.name: Grease-producing cooking without an approved hood and suppression
violations.law: NYC Fire Code 609 and Mechanical Code 507
violations.criminal: FDNY can order the equipment out of service; a fire with injuries can bring criminal charges.
violations.note: FDNY inspects and regulates required range hoods (NYC Business). Fine amounts are my game values: no official schedule was readable.

violations.name: Overdue hood cleaning or fire-suppression service
violations.note: A contractor blog gives $500-$1,000 for a first overdue cleaning or suppression inspection; FDNY's own schedule not seen.

violations.name: Propane handled without a G-23 Certificate of Fitness or truck permit
violations.note: FDNY requires a G-23 holder to connect LPG over one pound on carts and trucks and a $105 truck permit. Fine is my game value.

violations.name: Selling at a fair or market without a temporary food permit
violations.note: Market organizers check permits before load-in; the Health Department can close the stand for the day. Fine is my game value.

violations.name: Commercial cooking system operated without an FDNY permit
violations.note: The permit costs $70; the fine is my game value.

violations.name: Plastic straws given without a request
violations.law: NYC Local Law 64 of 2021; Admin Code 16-395
violations.note: Since November 1, 2021 food service establishments may give plastic straws only on request, free and without asking why; self-serve stations need a sign. Civil penalties $100-$400 per violation. Number seen in the web-search excerpt of this page on 2026-11-14; a direct fetch of the page was blocked by the session's network policy.

violations.name: Music or crowd noise from a commercial establishment
violations.law: NYC Admin Code 24-231 (commercial music); NYC Noise Code
violations.note: DEP fact sheet: a restaurant or bar may not exceed 42 dBA measured inside a dwelling that receives the noise; DEP can mitigate a first commercial-music violation to zero if a consultant certifies the fix (limiter). The dollar amounts in DEP's penalty schedule were not readable: base and max here are my game values. Complaints also weigh on the community board's view at license renewal.

violations.name: Cooked tapioca or dairy held too long at room temperature
violations.note: Time-as-a-control rules limit holding cooked starches outside temperature control to 4 hours; the fine is my game value from the general food-temperature range.

officials.name: Sanitation vending enforcement officer
officials.agency: NYC Department of Sanitation (DSNY) Street Vending Enforcement
officials.realProcess: Since 2024 vending enforcement sits with Sanitation. Officers measure distances to crosswalks and doors, check the license on the vendor's chest and the permit decal on the cart, write civil summonses and can remove the setup and discard food.

officials.name: Liquor Authority investigator
officials.agency: New York State Liquor Authority with NYPD
officials.realProcess: Underage operations send a decoy under 21 into licensed places; a sale brings disciplinary charges against the licensee and a summons for the server. Complaints from neighbours and the community board trigger visits.

officials.name: Fire inspector
officials.realProcess: FDNY inspects cooking exhaust and suppression systems, checks the tag from the last cleaning and service, and checks propane certificates on trucks and at commissaries. Violations come with a date to correct and fines when not corrected.

reports.name: Report an unlicensed or badly placed vendor (311)
reports.text: Sanitation sends vending enforcement. If the cart is legal and well placed, nothing happens.

reports.name: Report alcohol served to minors
reports.text: The Liquor Authority may run an underage check. If they card properly, it ends there.

reports.name: Report smoke and grease from a kitchen (311)
reports.text: FDNY inspects the hood and suppression tags. Clean records mean no action.

events.name: City opens new cart permit applications
events.text: Thousands of new street vending permits come in from 2026 to 2031. More carts appear on busy corners.
events.note: 2,200 supervisory license applications a year from 2026 through 2031 (Intro 431-B, enacted January 29, 2026). The 3% hit to a storefront cafe from new carts on its block is my estimate.

events.name: Liquor Authority backlog
events.text: New license applications take six months or more. Your temporary permit buys time, not certainty.
events.note: SLA notice: 24-26 weeks for new applications; some waited over a year. The demand effect applies only to a cafe waiting to add evening alcohol: my estimate.

events.name: Delivery apps push the enhanced plan
events.text: Apps offer top placement for up to 20% more commission. Restaurants that stay on the basic plan slide down the list.
events.note: Local Law 79 of 2025 (Intro 762-B) keeps the 23% cap for the basic plan and allows an optional enhanced tier up to 20% more. The 10% loss of delivery orders on the basic plan is my estimate.

events.name: Tariffs raise tapioca and tea costs
events.text: Pearls, tea and syrups come mostly from Taiwan and Southeast Asia. Import tariffs push your cost per drink up.
events.note: Market analysis (August 2025): key bubble tea inputs come from Taiwan or Southeast Asia and tariffs raise costs; a US boba maker said up to $1 more per drink. The US imported 38 million pounds of tapioca from Taiwan in 2024 (USITC). +8% on cost of goods is my estimate.

events.name: Con Edison shuts off gas to the building
events.text: A leak test finds bad piping upstairs. Gas stays off until the landlord's plumber passes a new test.
events.note: News 12: Con Ed shut off gas to a Fordham building after finding illegal plumbing work; the restaurant was told 6-8 months. Hits gas kitchens and bakeries; electric-only cafes are spared. The 15% loss (cold menu only) is my estimate.

ruleCards.title: Cart permits are capped
ruleCards.text: A NYC cart or truck permit costs $200 for two years but is capped. Since 2021, 445 new permits a year; from 2026 to 2031, 2,200 a year. Many vendors still rent a permit for up to $25,000.

ruleCards.title: Where a cart may stand
ruleCards.text: Next to the curb, at least 20 ft from a building entrance and 10 ft from a crosswalk, subway entrance or driveway, on a sidewalk at least 12 ft wide. Civil fines up to $250.

ruleCards.title: Every cart sleeps at a commissary
ruleCards.text: A permitted cart or truck must be cleaned, serviced and stored at a Health Department-approved commissary or depot. No commissary contract, no permit.

ruleCards.title: No selling at a meter
ruleCards.text: Food trucks may not sell while parked at a metered space (34 RCNY 4-08(h)(8)). Courts confirmed it in 2012. Expect tickets and tows.

ruleCards.title: Street vending fines are civil now
ruleCards.text: A 2025 law made most vending offenses civil: up to $250 for placement, up to $1,000 for vending without a license. Sanitation can still remove the setup.

ruleCards.title: Tell the community board first
ruleCards.text: Any on-premises liquor application in NYC needs 30 days' notice to the community board first. The board's vote is advisory, but its stipulations often end up in your license.

ruleCards.title: The 500-foot rule
ruleCards.text: A full liquor license near three or more bars within 500 ft needs a public-interest finding. Beer and wine only places are exempt.

ruleCards.title: Temporary permit while you wait
ruleCards.text: The SLA can issue a 180-day temporary permit while your license is pending: $640 for wine and liquor, $128 for beer only. You may not sell a drop before it is in hand.

ruleCards.title: Wine needs food
ruleCards.text: A Restaurant Wine license ($960 for two years in NYC plus $100 filing) requires a kitchen and a real menu. A pastry counter usually is not enough.

ruleCards.title: The city taxes your license too
ruleCards.text: NYC adds a tax equal to 25% of your annual state license fee, billed by the Department of Finance and due June 25.

ruleCards.title: One sale to a minor
ruleCards.text: First sale to a minor: $2,500-$4,000 civil penalty, up to $10,000. The licensee pays even if a new employee made the sale.

ruleCards.title: NYC caps delivery app fees
ruleCards.text: Apps may charge you 15% for delivery, 5% for listing and 3% for card processing. An optional enhanced plan adds up to 20% more.

ruleCards.title: Markets need their own permit
ruleCards.text: Your cafe permit covers your storefront only. Street fairs and markets need a $70 Temporary Food Service Establishment Permit and a certified supervisor on site.

ruleCards.title: Raw juice needs a warning
ruleCards.text: Juice you press and bottle for later sale must carry the unpasteurized warning label. Missing labels are cited at $400-$600.

ruleCards.title: Plastic straws on request
ruleCards.text: Plastic straws only when a customer asks, free, no questions. Self-serve stations need a sign. Fines $100-$400 per violation.

ruleCards.title: Hot food means a hood
ruleCards.text: Grease-producing cooking needs a Type I hood, a duct to the roof and a wet-chemical system installed under FDNY inspection, plus a $70 FDNY cooking permit.

ruleCards.title: Ventless ovens are not automatic
ruleCards.text: High-speed ventless ovens clean their own smoke, but NYC's DOB and FDNY decide whether one is allowed without a hood.

ruleCards.title: Bakeries can answer to the state
ruleCards.text: A mostly wholesale bakery is licensed by the State Department of Agriculture and Markets; a mostly retail one by the city Health Department. Let the state permit lapse and the city can close you.

ruleCards.title: Propane needs a certificate
ruleCards.text: On a cart or truck, only a holder of the FDNY G-23 Certificate of Fitness may hook up propane over one pound. Trucks also need a $105 FDNY permit.

ruleCards.title: Park kiosks pay a share
ruleCards.text: NYC Parks concessions pay the greater of a fixed annual minimum or 6%-11% of gross sales, under multi-year licenses won by proposal.

ruleCards.title: Wine to go, by the glass only
ruleCards.text: Licensed places may sell drinks to go through 2030, but only by the glass with a substantial food order; sealed bottles to go are not allowed under SLA guidance.

ruleCards.title: Outdoor drinks need a second approval
ruleCards.text: A DOT sidewalk cafe license does not cover alcohol. After DOT issues it, you file an alteration with the SLA within 60 days and serve outside only once the SLA approves.

ruleCards.title: Shared kitchen, your own permit
ruleCards.text: Renting time in a shared kitchen does not cover you: each business needs its own Food Service Establishment permit, and the kitchen may not rent to anyone without one.

ruleCards.title: Some streets are closed to carts
ruleCards.text: The Health Department publishes restricted streets by borough, day and hour where food vending is barred. Fines start at $50; general vending is barred in most of Midtown.

ruleCards.title: Vendors take their own course
ruleCards.text: Every cart or truck worker needs a $50 two-year license and the $53 Food Protection Course for Mobile Vendors with an exam. Fail and you pay again.

ruleCards.title: Incubator bakers pay no state fee
ruleCards.text: New York waives the $400 Article 20-C food processing license fee for two years for a first-time applicant working in a kitchen incubator.

ruleCards.title: Sandwiches are tavern food
ruleCards.text: For the SLA a restaurant serves full entree-style meals from a chef-run kitchen; a tavern must serve at least soups and sandwiches. A cafe with toasties usually applies for Tavern Wine.

ruleCards.title: Carts have a size limit
ruleCards.text: A sidewalk food cart may be at most about 5 ft wide and 10 ft long including wheels and signs, parked with its long side along the curb. Trucks are exempt from the size rule.

ruleCards.title: Station cafes pay a share
ruleCards.text: Transit kiosks and cafes are licensed by MTA Real Estate: a one-year Grand Central Madison pastry and coffee stall pays 15% of gross sales; larger station cafes pay base rent plus a share above a sales threshold.

roadmap.title: Pick a format before you pick a space
roadmap.text: A cart, a window, a bakery, a wine cafe and a delivery kitchen need different permits, power and capital. The format decides the space, not the other way round.

roadmap.title: Get on the cart permit list
roadmap.text: Take the mobile vendor food protection course, get your personal license, and register for the unit permit list. Check the Restricted Area option for private plazas.

roadmap.title: Sign a commissary contract
roadmap.text: No commissary, no permit. Compare storage, water, cleaning and how early you can roll out.

roadmap.title: Check power and gas before signing
roadmap.text: Ovens and kitchens need three-phase power or gas. Ask Con Edison about gas availability before you sign the lease.

roadmap.title: File the hood with DOB and the suppression with FDNY
roadmap.text: An engineer files the hood and duct with Buildings; a licensed fire suppression contractor installs and tests the wet-chemical system with an FDNY inspector.

roadmap.title: Notify the community board 30 days ahead
roadmap.text: Send the 30-day notice, fill the board questionnaire and attend the hearing before you file with the SLA.

roadmap.title: File the liquor application and the temporary permit together
roadmap.text: File the license and the 180-day temporary permit at the same time; the temporary permit lets you pour while the license waits.

roadmap.title: Choose delivery apps and the fee plan
roadmap.text: Basic plans are capped at 23% in NYC; enhanced plans can reach 43%. Price delivery menus for it.

suppliers.what: Overnight parking, water, cleaning and propane storage for carts and trucks
suppliers.whereToFind: DOHMH list of approved commissaries; ask vendors at the same corner
suppliers.note: A DOHMH requirement for every permitted unit.

suppliers.what: Hourly or monthly kitchen time with licensed space for delivery brands and wholesale baking
suppliers.whereToFind: Listing sites such as The Kitchen Door; incubators in Brooklyn and Queens
suppliers.note: Listings ran $25-$48 an hour; check the operator's finances (Pilotworks closed overnight in 2019).

suppliers.what: Tapioca pearls, tea leaves, syrups and wide straws
suppliers.whereToFind: US importers and distributors of Taiwanese ingredients
suppliers.note: Most inputs are imported; order 4-8 weeks ahead and expect tariff surcharges.

suppliers.what: Licensed wholesalers and distributors; retailers must pay within the legal credit period or go cash-only
suppliers.whereToFind: SLA-licensed wholesalers; distributor reps in your borough
suppliers.note: New York's credit law puts late payers on a delinquent list; wholesalers then sell to them only for cash.

suppliers.what: FDNY-approved duct cleaners and licensed fire suppression contractors
suppliers.whereToFind: FDNY lists of approved companies; ask the building's other restaurants
suppliers.note: Duct cleaning workers need a W-64/P-64 Certificate of Fitness.

formats.name: Takeaway window or counter-only coffee bar
formats.differsFromCafe: No seats, 150-300 sq ft, often a slice of a bigger storefront or a window onto the sidewalk. No customer restroom (the pack's 20-seat rule never triggers), no dining furniture, no table cleaning. Revenue is all takeaway: the sizing model's seats do not matter, the queue does. Rent is a third to a half of the cafe's for the same block, but the ticket is lower (drink only, few pastries) and nothing holds customers on a cold or rainy day.

startCost.note: Cafe pack minus the seating side: build-out 200 sq ft x $225 = $45,000 (setup.kiosk_buildout), espresso machine and grinder $9,700, refrigeration, sinks and smallwares about $6,000, deposit 3 x $3,000 rent, permits, opening stock and 2-3 months of working capital. My calculation, no published figure for NYC windows.

permits: Food Service Establishment Permit (DOHMH, $280 a year), same as the cafe
Food Protection Certificate
Sign permit if the sign is over 6 sq ft
No sidewalk cafe license: a window may not put tables out
formats.equipment: Same bar as the cafe (espresso machine, grinder, under-counter fridge, hand sink, three-compartment sink). Optional ventless oven for toasted items.
formats.staff: 1 barista most hours, 2 at the morning peak; the owner usually works the window.
formats.demand: Morning rush 7-10 a.m. carries the day; one barista at a two-group machine makes about 60-80 drinks an hour (cafe pack capacity). In January-February demand drops harder than for a seated cafe because nobody stays inside.
risks: Queue on the sidewalk in front of a neighbour's door: complaints and a landlord dispute
Weather: no indoor seats to shelter customers
Landlord carve-outs: a window inside another tenant's lease is a sublease that can end when that lease ends
Lower ticket: pastries sell less without a table
needsOwn: weather sensitivity higher than the cafe
queue penalty instead of crowd penalty

formats.name: Street coffee and breakfast cart
formats.differsFromCafe: No lease, no build-out: a $15,000 cart, a $50 personal license and a $200 two-year unit permit. But the permit is capped and was rationed by waiting lists for decades, so most carts work under a rented permit at $14,000-$25,000 per two years. The cart must sleep at a commissary, must stand next to the curb 20 ft from doors and 10 ft from crosswalks, and is enforced by Sanitation. Ticket is small (coffee $1.50-$3, bagel) and volume is all morning.

startCost.note: Cart $15,000 + generator $1,800 + commissary deposit $1,500 + license and permit $250 + G-23 $25 + first stock $1,500 + 3 months of working capital. With a rented permit add $14,000-$25,000 up front (Queens Eagle 2025).

permits: Mobile Food Vending License for every worker ($50 / 2 years)
Mobile Food Vending Unit Permit ($200 / 2 years, capped; 2,200 new applications a year 2026-2031)
Commissary agreement (approved non-retail food establishment)
FDNY G-23 Certificate of Fitness if propane is used
Restricted Area permit for private plazas (no cap)
formats.equipment: Cart with hand sink and water tanks, airpots or a compact espresso machine, generator or battery, cooler.
formats.staff: Owner alone or with one helper; the supervisory license holder must be present.
formats.demand: 7-10 a.m. office and commuter rush; a Midtown cart vendor said 9 a.m. is the busiest hour and coffee the best seller (Daily Meal). A Manhattan cart owner lost about half his customers after a $0.25 price rise (Business Insider, December 2025): extreme price sensitivity. An Upper East Side food cart made up to $1,300 a day in summer and $600 in winter before the pandemic, $300 after (West Side Rag 2021).
risks: Permit: renting is illegal and the holder can pull it any time; permit scammers target vendors (ABC7)
Sanitation enforcement sweeps, $250 placement fines, removal of the setup
Fights over the spot with storefront businesses and other vendors (ABC7, Upper West Side cart, November 2025)
Weather: rain and cold cut sales by half
Commissary closes or raises rent: no cart can operate without one
needsOwn: no sizing (hardCap by one worker's speed)

formats.name: Coffee or food truck
formats.differsFromCafe: Same capped DOHMH permit as a cart, plus a vehicle: $100,000-$175,000 new, commercial insurance, parking, fuel, propane under FDNY rules and a commissary. Trucks may not sell at metered spots (34 RCNY 4-08(h)(8)), which rules out most of Midtown's curb, and they pay the congestion toll entering Manhattan below 60th Street. Upside: it can follow events, offices on weekdays and parks on weekends.

startCost.note: Used fitted truck $90,000 (setup.food_truck_used) + permits and FDNY $400 + commissary deposit $1,500 + wrap and menu $5,000 + stock and working capital; a new truck $100,000-$175,000 (Start Business by State 2026).

permits: Mobile Food Vending License and Unit Permit (capped)
FDNY LPG truck permit $105 and G-23 Certificate of Fitness
DMV registration and commercial auto insurance
Commissary
formats.equipment: Truck with generator, espresso or grill line, refrigeration, water tanks, fire extinguisher 20:B-C.
formats.demand: Lunch and events; weekday office districts, weekend markets and festivals. Event fees and parking decide the margin.
risks: Meter rule: tickets and tows in metered zones (CBS, Midtown crackdowns)
Vehicle breakdown stops the whole business
Congestion toll and parking tickets as a monthly cost
Permit market as for carts

formats.name: Bakery-cafe (bakes on site)
formats.differsFromCafe: Ovens, mixers, proofers and night or dawn labor. Pastry becomes the main product instead of a 2% side line, so the ticket rises and cost of goods follows flour, butter and egg prices. Gas ovens need a gas authorization and a Con Edison turn-on that has taken months; three-phase electric ovens need the panel for it. If wholesale to other cafes is more than half the business, the State Department of Agriculture and Markets licenses it (Article 20-C, $400 for two years) instead of the city Health Department.

startCost.note: Cafe pack $224,000 + convection oven $8,086 + spiral mixer $9,000 + proofer $4,500 + extra refrigeration and benches $8,000 + hood or ventilation where needed $0-$45,000 + gas work $3,500 + 2 more months of build-out rent while ovens are installed. My calculation.

permits: FSE permit (retail) or NYS Ag & Markets Article 20-C license (wholesale majority, $400 / 2 years)
DOB permits for ovens and ventilation; gas authorization
FDNY cooking permit $70 if under a Type I hood
formats.equipment: Convection or deck oven, spiral mixer, proofer/retarder, sheeter (later), walk-in or extra reach-ins, bakers' benches.
formats.staff: 1-2 bakers starting 3-5 a.m. plus counter staff; bakers are the hardest hire and the most expensive hours.
formats.demand: Morning and weekend; holiday orders (Thanksgiving pies, Christmas) are the year's peaks; wholesale accounts smooth the week.
risks: Ingredient swings: eggs averaged $5.69 a dozen in Q1 2025 and $2.27 in September 2026 (BLS via FRED); butter averaged a record $2.88/lb in 2024 and $1.54 in July 2026 (CME)
Gas delays or a building gas shutoff stop the ovens
Night labor and burnout
Two-agency trap: a wholesale bakery whose state permit lapsed was closed by the city (Duane Park Patisserie, October 2025)
Waste: unsold pastry at closing
reusesFromCafe: whole cafe pack: coffee bar, FSE permit, staff.barista, levers, violations
needsOwn: cogs linked to egg, butter and flour indices
oven capacity as a second capacity limit
wholesale channel and the 51% agency switch

formats.name: Sandwich bar / deli counter
formats.differsFromCafe: Lunch instead of breakfast: the peak moves to 12-2 p.m. and the ticket doubles ($13-$17). Cost of goods rises to about a third of sales (meat, cheese, bread, produce) and prep labor grows: slicing, assembly, morning prep. Cold sandwiches need only a refrigerated prep table and a slicer; hot pressed sandwiches need a ventless oven or a hood. Catering trays for offices are a second channel.

startCost.note: Cafe pack minus part of the coffee bar + prep table $1,329 + slicer $619 + second reach-in + ventless oven $17,190 or hood $45,000 + bigger opening stock. My calculation.

permits: FSE permit and Food Protection Certificate (same as cafe)
FDNY cooking permit and hood only if grilling or frying
formats.equipment: Refrigerated sandwich prep table, slicer, reach-in fridges, toaster or ventless oven, bread rack.
formats.staff: 2-4 at lunch: sandwich makers are faster to train than baristas but the line needs more hands at noon.
formats.demand: Office lunch, strongly tied to how many days a week offices are full; catering for meetings.
risks: Slicer cuts and Listeria if the slicer is not cleaned
Meat and cheese price swings
Office attendance on Mondays and Fridays
Competition from delis and bodegas already on every block
reusesFromCafe: FSE permit, health violations, staff structure, levers.cleaning, card fees, insurance

formats.name: Juice and smoothie bar
formats.differsFromCafe: Produce instead of coffee: cost of goods is far higher and spoils in days. A cold-press juicer costs about $11,900; blenders are loud. Juice pressed and bottled for later sale must carry the unpasteurized warning label (fines $400-$600) and may need a HACCP plan approved by DOHMH. Demand peaks in January (resolutions, cleanses) and in summer heat, and is fashion-driven: NYC chains shrank sharply (Organic Avenue closed in 2015, Liquiteria shut, Juice Press closed East Village and Greenwich Street stores in 2025-2026).

startCost.note: Cafe-style build-out of a smaller space + juicer $11,900 + blenders $1,900 + walk-in or extra reach-ins + sealer $1,800. My calculation.

permits: FSE permit; HACCP plan if bottling juice for later sale
Unpasteurized juice warning label (Health Code Article 81, 21 CFR 101.17(g))
formats.equipment: Cold-press juicer, commercial blenders with enclosures, produce washing sink, reach-in fridges, bottle sealer or capper.
formats.staff: 2 at peaks; daily produce prep before opening.
formats.demand: January and June-August peaks; affluent residential and gym-adjacent blocks; fragile to fashion.
risks: Spoilage: produce lasts days, juice has a short shelf life
Fashion cycle and chain collapses
Label and HACCP violations
High ticket ($9-$13) with low repeat outside peaks

formats.name: Bubble tea shop
formats.differsFromCafe: Cheaper bar (no $7,600 espresso machine, no $2,000 grinders) but a different supply chain: tapioca pearls, tea and syrups are imported mostly from Taiwan and Southeast Asia, so tariffs and shipping move the cost per drink. Pearls are cooked in batches and lose texture within hours, which forces discards. Customers are students and young adults, the peak is afternoon and evening, and wide plastic straws run into the city's on-request straw law.

startCost.note: Small storefront build-out + sealer $1,800 + pearl cooker and dispensers $4,500 + blenders $1,900 + ice machine $3,500 + refrigeration; franchise brands add a fee. My calculation.

permits: FSE permit and Food Protection Certificate (same as cafe)
Straws: plastic only on request (Local Law 64 of 2021)
formats.equipment: Sealer, pearl cooker, tea brewers, fructose dispenser, blenders, ice machine, shaker station.
formats.staff: 2-3 per shift; fast to train; open late.
formats.demand: Afternoon and evening, summer peak, near schools and universities; delivery share high.
risks: Tariffs on Taiwanese inputs
Saturation: chains open near each other
Time-temperature rules for cooked pearls
Straw law fines $100-$400
reusesFromCafe: FSE permit, health violations, levers.cleaning, staff wage rules, delivery mechanics

formats.name: Cafe by day, wine and beer by night
formats.differsFromCafe: The same room earns a second shift: 5-10 p.m. wine and beer at a $14-$18 ticket. The price is a state license and time: Restaurant Wine is $960 for two years in NYC plus $100 filing (and requires a kitchen and a real menu), a 30-day community board notice comes first, new applications took 24-26 weeks, and the 180-day temporary permit ($640) bridges part of the wait. Then come evening labor, liquor liability insurance, underage stings and neighbours' noise complaints.

startCost.note: On top of the cafe: license $1,060 + temporary permit $640 + lawyer $5,000 + wine and beer fit-out $6,000 + opening wine stock $4,000 + menu and kitchen upgrade to qualify (ventless oven $17,190 when needed). My calculation.

permits: SLA Tavern Wine license (soups and sandwiches; about $1,252 / 2 years, estimate) or Restaurant Wine ($960 + $100; full meals and a chef-run kitchen)
SLA Temporary Retail Permit
30-day community board notice
NYC retail liquor license tax (25% of the annual fee)
Kitchen and menu that satisfy the SLA
formats.equipment: Wine fridge, kegerator, glassware, simple hot food line.
formats.staff: Evening server-bartender; anyone serving must be 18+; owner or manager on site for license compliance.
formats.demand: Thursday-Saturday evenings; neighbourhoods with residents rather than office districts.
risks: License wait: 6-12 months with rent running
Community board stipulations: closing hours, no outdoor drinks
Underage sale: $2,500-$4,000 first offense
Dram shop liability
Noise complaints near apartments
reusesFromCafe: everything; this is the cafe with a second shift
needsOwn: second daypart with its own demand and ticket

formats.name: Delivery-only kitchen (shared or ghost kitchen)
formats.differsFromCafe: No storefront, no walk-in customers, no foot traffic: all orders come through apps that keep 23% (basic plan) to 43% (enhanced plan) of each order under NYC's caps. Rent is hours in a shared kitchen ($25-$48 an hour in Brooklyn and Queens listings) or a station in a ghost kitchen. Visibility is the app's ranking, not the street. The operator can disappear overnight: Pilotworks locked out 175 food businesses in Brooklyn in 2019; Reef closed its three New York ghost kitchens.

startCost.note: Kitchen onboarding $3,500 + small equipment $5,000 + packaging and tablets $1,500 + permits + photography and launch promotions $5,000 + 3 months of working capital. My calculation.

permits: Each business still needs its own DOHMH permit or must operate under the shared kitchen's arrangement
Food Protection Certificate
Insurance certificate naming the kitchen
formats.equipment: Mostly the kitchen's; you bring smallwares, packaging, label printer.
formats.demand: Evening and weekend delivery; ranking falls without promotions; ratings drive everything.
risks: Commission 23%-43%
Operator closure (Pilotworks 2019)
Algorithm changes
No walk-in fallback
reusesFromCafe: FSE rules, food safety violations, staff wage rules
needsOwn: no footTraffic; demand = app impressions x conversion

formats.name: Market stall or pop-up (street fairs, Smorgasburg, holiday markets)
formats.differsFromCafe: A weekend or seasonal stand instead of a lease: a $70 annual Temporary Food Service Establishment permit, a tent and the market's fee. Markets choose vendors by application and demand weekly commitment (vendors who miss a day still pay). It is how many NYC food brands test a product before signing a lease.

startCost.note: Tent and gear $2,500 + permit $70 + G-23 if propane + first market fees + stock. An older profile priced a Smorgasburg 10x10 stall at $120-$225 a day; electricity adds $50 a day (Appear Here).

permits: Temporary Food Service Establishment Permit ($70 / year)
Food Protection Certificate holder on site
FDNY G-23 for propane
formats.equipment: Tent, tables, coolers, hand-wash station, generator or market power.
formats.demand: Weekends April-October; November-December holiday markets; rain cancels.
risks: Weather cancellations still cost the fee
Market selection: not accepted next season
Commissary or licensed kitchen still needed for prep
needsOwn: days-per-month instead of a full month

formats.name: Kiosk in a park, plaza or inside another business
formats.differsFromCafe: No market rent: you pay the owner the greater of a guaranteed minimum or a share of gross sales (NYC Parks: 6%-11%; Harlem Meer snack bar 9% vs $20,000 in year 1; Cadman Plaza cafe 10%). Spots are won by proposal (RFP) for multi-year terms; a business improvement district or park conservancy can run its own kiosk RFPs (Bryant Park 2024, The Battery 2025). Footfall is the park's: huge in summer weekends, thin in winter. Transit stations work the same way: MTA Real Estate licensed a one-year coffee and pastry stall at Grand Central Madison for 15% of gross sales (2025), and a White Plains station coffee concession for $111,000 base rent plus 10% of sales above $1.14 million.

startCost.note: Kiosk fit-out often partly provided; equipment $15,000-$25,000, concession deposit $10,000, proposal preparation, working capital for the slow first winter. My calculation.

permits: FSE permit or Restricted Area mobile permit
Concession license from NYC Parks or the private owner
Parks rules on hours, menu and signage
formats.equipment: Same bar as the takeaway window.
formats.demand: Weekend and summer heavy; events in the park; winter closure in many kiosks.
risks: Guaranteed minimum due even in a bad season
License not renewed at the end of the term
Owner's rules on menu and prices
Seasonal closure
needsOwn: RFP win as a roadmap step

permits: Check DOB/FDNY acceptance of the UL 710B listing
DOB mechanical filing for hood and duct
FDNY suppression installation and acceptance test
FDNY Commercial Cooking System permit $70
Gas authorization if gas

transitions.note: A cafe that wants hot sandwiches picks a ventless oven (one purchase, light-duty food only) or a Type I hood (heavy work, a roof duct, often the landlord's consent and weeks with the counter closed). The landlord's lease must allow cooking: many retail leases forbid 'cooking with open flame or grease-producing equipment'.

steps: SLA application with floor plan and menu
License ($960 + $100 for two years, 24-26 weeks or more)
NYC license tax, liquor liability insurance, staff training
transitions.note: Costs from the SLA fee chart and TRP form; the $15,000 adds the lawyer, fit-out and opening stock (my estimate).

A second site repeats the whole setup (new lease, deposit, build-out, its own FSE permit: permits are per address) and needs a manager at the first site ($4,800 a month in the cafe pack) because the owner can no longer stand behind both counters. Shared purchasing and one roaster contract save a few points of cost of goods.

The usual graduation path: the cart proves a following, then a window lease. The cart permit and the storefront FSE permit are separate; a supervisory license holder must still work the cart if it stays open.

mechanics.title: Choose the food format at the start
mechanics.playerDecision: Before picking a space, the player picks a format: cafe, takeaway window, cart, truck, bakery-cafe, sandwich bar, juice bar, bubble tea, cafe-wine bar, delivery kitchen, market stall or park kiosk.
mechanics.engineMath: The format loads the cafe pack and applies extra.formats[].packOverrides (startCapital, unit.refPrice, unit.cogsPerUnit, sizing.takeawayShare) plus the format's own setup items (setup[].formats contains the format id). Rent comes from the place, except: cart/truck -> monthlyCosts.commissary_fee; delivery_kitchen -> shared_kitchen_hours; concession_kiosk -> max(minimum, concession_share x revenue). Demand: footTraffic-based for storefront formats; delivery_kitchen uses deliveryShare = 1 and ignores footTraffic.
fieldsNeeded: hourly demand profile by format (breakfast, lunch, afternoon, evening)

mechanics.title: The cart permit queue and the permit black market
mechanics.playerDecision: A cart player either waits for the city's permit list (no sales meanwhile, or sells only on private property with a Restricted Area permit) or rents someone else's permit now (shortcut rent_vending_permit).
mechanics.engineMath: Legal path: the permit arrives after N months, where N falls each fiscal year from July 2026 to 2031 as 2,200 new applications open (announced to all players in advance). Black-market path: monthly cost black_market_permit_rent ($850), immediate sales; violation permit_holder_absent can be found by dsny_vendor_officer inspection or a rival's report; on finding: fine, cart removed for closureDays, and the permit is lost (back to the queue). Restricted Area path: no queue, but demand x 0.6 (private plazas only) plus a fee to the owner (lever cart_spot).
fieldsNeeded: shortcut.unlocks (a shortcut that buys time instead of money)

mechanics.title: Adding evening wine and beer: the license clock
mechanics.playerDecision: Apply to add alcohol (lever alcohol_program); choose whether to wait for the temporary permit or pour early (shortcut pour_before_license).
mechanics.engineMath: Month 0: community board notice (30 days). Month 1: SLA filing + TRP application ($100 + $960 + $640). TRP arrives about 2 months later and lasts 6 months; license arrives at month 1 + 6 to 12 (announced range; the exact month is set at filing, no dice). While licensed: a second daypart opens with its own demand (evening residents) and ticket $16, cogs 30%; costs: evening labor, liquor_liability_insurance, nyc_liquor_license_tax once a year. Community board stipulations cap closing time (options wine_beer_late unavailable if the board stipulated 10 p.m.).
fieldsNeeded: dayparts: separate demand and ticket per daypart

mechanics.title: Hot food: ventless oven or a real hood
mechanics.playerDecision: Lever hot_food: cold only, ventless oven ($17,190, no works) or a full Type I hood ($45,000, months of works).
mechanics.engineMath: Ventless: one setup purchase, demand +6%, quality +0.02, ticket +$1.50; menu limited (no frying). Hood: setup $45,000 + 2-3 months of partial operation (counter open, kitchen closed), FDNY permit and $250 a month of cleaning and suppression service; skipping the service (shortcut skip_suppression_service) triggers suppression_overdue after 3 months and, with grease build-up, a kitchen fire event that closes the shop (the fire is a consequence, not a dice roll: it happens in the announced month if the service was skipped for 6 months).
fieldsNeeded: deferred consequence after N months of a shortcut

mechanics.title: Delivery apps: capped commission and the enhanced tier
mechanics.playerDecision: Lever delivery_plan: no apps, basic plan, or enhanced plan.
mechanics.engineMath: Delivery revenue = deliveryShare x demand x ticket. Fee = 23% (basic) or up to 43% (enhanced) of delivery revenue (monthlyCosts.delivery_app_commission). Enhanced plan raises deliveryShare; the event delivery_enhanced_tier lowers deliveryShare for basic-plan players. For delivery_kitchen, deliveryShare = 1 and footTraffic is ignored.

mechanics.title: Opening a second location
mechanics.playerDecision: After month 6 with positive cash, the player may open a second site.
mechanics.engineMath: The second site is a new business object with its own place, setup, lease and FSE permit (permits are per address). The owner can staff only one counter: the first site needs the manager (manager.monthlySalary) or loses the owner's quality bonus. Shared purchasing: cogs x 0.97 at both sites. Cash is shared, so a bad second site can sink the first one.

mechanics.title: Concession rent: the greater of a minimum or a share of sales
mechanics.playerDecision: Bid for a park or plaza kiosk: choose the share of sales and the guaranteed minimum to offer.
mechanics.engineMath: Monthly rent = max(minimum / 12, share x revenue). Higher bids win the spot (other players or a fixed city reserve); the winner is locked in for the license term.
