eventCatalog.name: New cart permits become available
eventCatalog.text: The city opens a new round of supervisory license applications for street food vendors. Expect more carts on busy corners from next month.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DOHMH/DCWP invitation round under Intro 431-B (January 2026): 2,200 supervisory license applications a year, fiscal years 2027-2031
eventCatalog.note: The 2,200 figure is from the law as reported; the 2% capture loss for storefronts on vendor-heavy blocks and the 30% shorter queue are my estimates.

eventCatalog.name: Sanitation vending sweep on your corridor
eventCatalog.text: Sanitation and police sweep the avenue: carts too close to crosswalks are ticketed and some setups are removed.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DSNY Street Vending Enforcement operations; Roosevelt Avenue crackdown, spring 2025
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Several times a year on busy corridors
eventCatalog.note: Queens Eagle (April 2025): the Roosevelt Avenue crackdown pushed vendors toward black-market permits. Legal, well-placed carts lose only the days of disruption (my 20% estimate).

eventCatalog.name: Your permit holder wants it back
eventCatalog.text: The person whose permit you rent wants double, or plans to sell it to someone else at the end of the two-year cycle.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Two-year permit cycle; Queens Eagle reports of $14,000-$25,000 per cycle
eventCatalog.realFrequency: At each two-year renewal for rented permits
eventCatalog.note: Follows from the player's choice to rent a permit; the cart stops until a new permit or a Restricted Area spot is found.

eventCatalog.name: A 'permit broker' offers a fast permit
eventCatalog.text: A stranger offers to get you a cart permit in two weeks for $3,000 cash up front.
eventCatalog.realSignal: ABC7 report on a scammer targeting NYC street food vendors
eventCatalog.note: A choice event: paying loses the cash and brings no permit. The legal route is the DOHMH list or a Restricted Area permit.

eventCatalog.name: Your commissary raises its fee
eventCatalog.text: Your depot raises the monthly fee by a third. Carts cannot legally operate without a commissary.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Commissary price lists; DOHMH requirement of an approved commissary for every unit
eventCatalog.note: The size of the rise is my estimate; the requirement is from DOHMH.

eventCatalog.name: Midtown meter crackdown
eventCatalog.text: Traffic agents ticket and tow food trucks selling from metered spots in Midtown.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Enforcement of 34 RCNY 4-08(h)(8); CBS New York report on trucks chased from Midtown
eventCatalog.note: Monroy v. City of New York (2012) confirmed the rule applies to food trucks.

eventCatalog.name: Congestion toll for the truck
eventCatalog.text: Every weekday trip into Manhattan below 60th Street pays the congestion toll.
eventCatalog.realSignal: MTA Congestion Relief Zone toll (since January 5, 2025): passenger vehicles $9 at peak; trucks about $14-$22
eventCatalog.note: Add about $14.40 x 20 weekdays = $288 a month for a small truck working Midtown; vans tolled as passenger cars pay $9. Amounts from Geotab's summary, to be checked against MTA tables.

eventCatalog.name: The truck breaks down
eventCatalog.text: The generator dies on the hottest week. The truck sits in the shop for ten days.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Follows four months on the 'fix it when it breaks' maintenance option
eventCatalog.note: Ten lost days of thirty = demand x 0.65; repair about $3,000; my estimates.

eventCatalog.name: FDNY checks propane on carts and trucks
eventCatalog.text: Fire inspectors check G-23 certificates and cylinder sizes at a street fair and on your route.
eventCatalog.realSignal: FDNY enforcement of the G-23 rule and LPG truck permits
eventCatalog.note: FDNY: only a G-23 holder may connect LPG over one pound to a cart or truck; trucks may carry at most two cylinders of 100 lb.

eventCatalog.name: Heat advisory: iced drinks fly, hot coffee stalls
eventCatalog.text: The heat index tops 95°F two days running. Bubble tea and juice sell out; nobody wants a hot latte from a cart.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NWS heat advisory for NYC: heat index 95-99°F for 2 consecutive days or 100-104°F for any duration
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Several advisories each summer (NWS Upton issued one on May 19, 2026)
eventCatalog.note: Criteria from NWS and NYC Emergency Management; the demand multipliers are my estimates.

eventCatalog.name: January resolutions
eventCatalog.text: Everyone is on a cleanse. Juice and smoothie orders jump for three weeks, then fall back.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Seasonal search and sales peak for juice cleanses each January
eventCatalog.note: No public NYC sales series was found; the size is my estimate and needs data (see 'not found').

eventCatalog.name: Produce costs jump
eventCatalog.text: Greens, berries and citrus cost more this month after a bad harvest in California and Mexico.
eventCatalog.realSignal: BLS CPI 'fresh fruits and vegetables' index month over month
eventCatalog.note: Signal is the CPI series; the 8% size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Egg prices spike (bird flu)
eventCatalog.text: Avian flu culls laying hens. Eggs cost more than double last year's price; every croissant and custard costs more.
eventCatalog.realSignal: BLS average price, eggs grade A large (FRED APU0000708111) above $4 a dozen
eventCatalog.note: Prices seen in the FRED data excerpt; the 6% cost-of-goods effect for a bakery (eggs about 10% of its ingredient cost) is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Butter gets cheap
eventCatalog.text: Butter on the Chicago exchange drops to $1.54 a pound, about half of 2024's record. Laminated pastry gets cheaper to make.
eventCatalog.realSignal: CME Grade AA butter cash price
eventCatalog.note: Prices from USDA/CME reports in the search excerpt; the 4% effect is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Tariffs on Taiwanese ingredients
eventCatalog.text: New import duties hit pearls, tea and syrups. Your distributor adds a surcharge.
eventCatalog.realSignal: US tariff schedule on imports from Taiwan; distributor surcharges
eventCatalog.note: Inputs mostly from Taiwan or Southeast Asia; a US boba maker spoke of up to $1 more per drink (KTVU). The 8% is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Back to school
eventCatalog.text: Students are back. Afternoon lines return to the bubble tea counter.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYC public school calendar and university terms
eventCatalog.note: Size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Straw law checks
eventCatalog.text: Consumer protection inspectors visit drink shops to check that plastic straws are only given on request.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DCWP enforcement of Local Law 64 of 2021
eventCatalog.note: Fines $100-$400 per violation.

eventCatalog.name: Con Edison gas turn-on delayed
eventCatalog.text: Your ovens are installed, but Con Edison says the building's service needs new piping. Gas could take months.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison gas availability answer for the address; DOB gas authorization status
eventCatalog.realFrequency: A 2017 NY Senate survey: only 17% of businesses got gas on time
eventCatalog.note: Follows the player's choice of gas equipment in a space without confirmed gas. Lucky Bee cooked on induction for three months (DNAinfo 2016).

eventCatalog.name: Gas shut off for the whole building
eventCatalog.text: A leak test upstairs fails. Con Edison locks the gas meter until the landlord's plumber passes a new test.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Con Edison shutoff after failed leak test or illegal piping
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Several per year in old buildings
eventCatalog.note: News 12: a Fordham restaurant was told 6-8 months. Electric-only kitchens keep running.

eventCatalog.name: Liquor Authority backlog
eventCatalog.text: New applications are taking six months or more. Your temporary permit may run out first.
eventCatalog.realSignal: SLA notice on processing time for new applications: 24-26 weeks
eventCatalog.note: Some NYC applications stayed open more than a year (Rodriguez Law).

eventCatalog.name: Community board asks for a 10 p.m. close
eventCatalog.text: The board backs your liquor application on conditions: close by 10 p.m., no drinks on the sidewalk, no live music.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Community board SLA committee resolution on the application
eventCatalog.note: Boards are advisory; the SLA often writes the stipulations into the license method of operation.

eventCatalog.name: Temporary permit about to expire
eventCatalog.text: Your 180-day temporary permit runs out next month and the license is still pending.
eventCatalog.realSignal: SLA temporary retail permit term (180 days since 2024) and extension rules
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Whenever the license outruns the permit
eventCatalog.note: The SLA form lists 30- and 60-day extensions (for beer-only: $64 and $128).

eventCatalog.name: Underage decoy operation
eventCatalog.text: The Liquor Authority and police send under-21 decoys into licensed places across the borough this month.
eventCatalog.realSignal: SLA press releases on underage drinking operations
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Several operations a year per region
eventCatalog.note: Penalty from SLA: $2,500-$4,000 first offense, up to $10,000.

eventCatalog.name: Neighbours complain about late nights
eventCatalog.text: Upstairs tenants call 311 about voices and music after 10 p.m. DEP measures the noise in their apartment.
eventCatalog.realSignal: 311 noise complaints; DEP 42 dBA limit in a dwelling for commercial music
eventCatalog.note: DEP fact sheet: commercial establishments may not exceed 42 dBA measured inside a dwelling; DEP can mitigate a first violation to zero if the owner fixes it (limiter, consultant).

eventCatalog.name: Apps push the enhanced plan
eventCatalog.text: Delivery apps move enhanced-plan restaurants to the top of the list. Basic-plan kitchens lose orders.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Local Law 79 of 2025: optional enhanced services up to 20% on top of the 23% basic cap
eventCatalog.note: The size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: City reviews delivery fee caps
eventCatalog.text: Consumer protection asks restaurants for feedback on the delivery fee caps. Changes could follow next year.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DCWP fee-cap feedback flyer, April 2026
eventCatalog.note: An announcement event with no immediate effect.

eventCatalog.name: Your shared kitchen shuts overnight
eventCatalog.text: The kitchen operator emails tenants that it is closing today. Your stock is inside and orders are queued.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Operator insolvency; Pilotworks Brooklyn closed with hours of notice in October 2019 (175 businesses)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Rare, but repeated (Pilotworks 2019; Reef closed three NY sites)
eventCatalog.note: Announced-in-advance rule: the game announces the operator's trouble a month ahead (missed payments, staff layoffs) so the player can move.

eventCatalog.name: Ghost kitchen operator leaves New York
eventCatalog.text: The company running your ghost kitchen files to close its New York sites at the end of next month.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NY State WARN notice filings by kitchen operators
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Reef: three NY sites, 53 workers, closure on September 30
eventCatalog.note: WARN filings give the advance notice the game needs.

eventCatalog.name: Outdoor market season opens
eventCatalog.text: Weekend food markets reopen in parks and waterfronts. Booths are booked by application.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Smorgasburg and other markets announce new-season vendors in spring
eventCatalog.note: Size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Holiday markets
eventCatalog.text: Six weeks of holiday markets in parks and plazas: the year's busiest booths, at the year's highest fees.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Holiday market booth calendars (Bryant Park, Union Square, Columbus Circle)
eventCatalog.note: Booth fees were not found in public sources (see 'not found').

eventCatalog.name: Street fair season
eventCatalog.text: Weekend street fairs close avenues and fill them with vendor booths, many with a $70 temporary food permit.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Street Activity Permit Office (SAPO) street fair calendar
eventCatalog.note: Documented (April 2025): street fair vendors no longer need a separate DCWP temporary vendor permit.

eventCatalog.name: Rainy weekends
eventCatalog.text: The forecast shows rain on two of four weekends. Markets run, but crowds stay home.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NWS climate normals: about 10-11 days with measurable precipitation per month in Central Park
eventCatalog.note: Normal rain days are climatology, announced as the month's expected weather; the size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Park kiosk license up for bid
eventCatalog.text: The Parks Department or a park conservancy invites proposals for a coffee kiosk: a share of sales against a guaranteed minimum.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYC Parks concessions RFP listings; conservancy RFPs (Bryant Park 2024, The Battery 2025)
eventCatalog.note: A choice event: bid share and minimum (mechanic concession_fee_floor).

eventCatalog.name: Thanksgiving and holiday orders
eventCatalog.text: Pie and bread pre-orders pour in for the holiday week. Ovens run around the clock.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Holiday calendar
eventCatalog.note: Size is my estimate; capacity is the oven, not the counter.

eventCatalog.name: State bakery license lapses
eventCatalog.text: Your State Agriculture license expired last month. A city inspector says you now need a city permit, and writes you up.
eventCatalog.realSignal: NYS Agriculture and Markets license expiry for a mostly-wholesale bakery
eventCatalog.note: Tribeca Citizen: state permit expired August 14, 2025; city violation September 8; closed October 20; reopened after applying for a city permit and passing inspection.

eventCatalog.name: Deli meat recall
eventCatalog.text: Your deli meat brand is recalled nationwide. You pull it, throw it out and switch suppliers; customers avoid cold cuts for a week.
eventCatalog.realSignal: USDA FSIS recall notices
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Boar's Head recalled about 7 million lb in July 2024
eventCatalog.note: A blog citing the episode said all deli meat sales fell almost 8% the week the recall was announced; secondary source.

eventCatalog.name: Offices fill up again
eventCatalog.text: Big employers in Midtown move to four or five office days. Weekday lunch lines get longer.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Manhattan office vacancy fell to 19.3% (Cushman & Wakefield, Q2 2026); availability 13.0%, lowest since October 2020 (Colliers)
eventCatalog.note: Vacancy is a proxy; no 2026 badge-swipe data was found. Size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: A storefront fights your cart's spot
eventCatalog.text: The shop behind your corner calls 311 every morning and asks the landlord to put planters on the sidewalk.
eventCatalog.realSignal: 311 vendor complaints; ABC7 'Street vendors fight to keep their coffee cart's spot' (November 2025)
eventCatalog.note: The Upper West Side cart in ABC7's story was back in its spot within 24 hours after 30 years on the block.

eventCatalog.name: Regulars balk at a 25-cent rise
eventCatalog.text: You add a quarter to a cart coffee. Half the regulars walk to the next cart.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Business Insider as-told-to essay, Midtown coffee cart owner, December 2025
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Follows a price rise at a low-ticket cart
eventCatalog.note: The owner said he lost about half his customers after a $0.25 rise. Implies a cart's price elasticity far above the cafe pack's.

eventCatalog.name: Outdoor tables, but no wine outside yet
eventCatalog.text: Your sidewalk cafe license came through, but outdoor drinks wait for the Liquor Authority to approve your alteration filing.
eventCatalog.realSignal: SLA alteration application after DOT Dining Out NYC approval (45-60 day SLA review in 2025 reporting)
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Every spring for new sidewalk cafes
eventCatalog.note: In 2025 only 7 of about 3,000 applicants had full approval at one point; the SLA then allowed drinks at setups with DOT conditional approval while its review ran (Streetsblog, DOT press release).

eventCatalog.name: Permit holder must stand at the cart
eventCatalog.text: The city starts checking that the supervisory license holder is at each cart. Rented-permit carts get caught.
eventCatalog.realSignal: DOHMH supervisory license rules (Local Law 18 of 2021); 'Supervisory licenses: what vendors need to know'
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Ongoing as supervisory licenses roll out
eventCatalog.note: The size of the inspection rise is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: A grab-and-go chain moves in
eventCatalog.text: An app-first coffee chain takes the small to-go space down the block. It sells mostly through its own app, with no seats.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Broker reports: Luckin Coffee opened nine NYC stores in seven months and targets small to-go spaces vacated by Starbucks
eventCatalog.realFrequency: Several openings a year in Manhattan
eventCatalog.note: Size is my estimate; the chain's own app discounts are the threat to a window, not seats.

eventCatalog.name: The chain store on the corner closes
eventCatalog.text: The national chain shuts its store nearby. Its morning regulars look for a new place.
eventCatalog.realSignal: Starbucks closing 42 NYC locations (about 12% of its city total) in its 2025 restructuring
eventCatalog.note: ABC7 and amNY on the closures; Dunkin' became Manhattan's largest chain. Size is my estimate.

eventCatalog.name: Station stalls up for bid
eventCatalog.text: MTA Real Estate releases individual requests for proposals for food stalls in a busy terminal: one-year licenses paid as a share of sales.
eventCatalog.realSignal: MTA Real Estate RFPs and board staff summaries (Grand Central Madison moved from one master vendor to individual stall RFPs)
eventCatalog.note: A choice event: bid a share of gross sales (15% in a 2025 one-year Grand Central Madison license) for a commuter-heavy stall.
